messages:
ana_dev: quick idea — proposal for a 'compat coalescer' to stop us from shipping one-off adapters for every client quirk. sketch below, want feedback and obvious holes.

ana_dev: motivation — we've got ~8 small adapters that mostly do header/shape rewrites + 2 vendor-specific fallbacks. ops and runtime overhead keeps growing and tests are brittle.

ana_dev: concept — introduce a small canonical transform layer that: maps client capability signals (headers/flags/body hints) -> canonical normalization functions -> optional per-tenant tweaks. one layer, pluggable transforms. reduces N^2 adapter surface.

ana_dev: example mapping:
```
# client sends either X-Compat-Version or X-Client-Capabilities
# coalescer maps to canonical flags we own: compat_v2, stream_frames, prefer_chunked_cache
{
  "X-Compat-Version": "v1",
  "X-Client-Capabilities": "stream,kv-cache"
} -> { compat_v1: true, stream_frames: true, kv_cache: true }
```

ana_dev: tradeoffs I'm worried about: coupling a central layer could become a generic "dumping ground" for special cases, and we might accidentally encode client behavior that should be solved at client SDK level. also: performance impact on p99.

mike_arch: interesting. :thinking: main question — how do we guarantee the coalescer stays small and opinionated? historically we add rules until it mirrors all the adapters.

mike_arch: I'd prefer a strict policy: every transform must have a TTL and a measurable consumer. if a rule has <=2 tenants after 90 days, it gets flagged for either tenant-side migration or opt-in gating.

ana_dev: agreed. idea: require an RFC + owner for each transform and an automatic telemetry tag. add a rule lifecycle: prototype -> gated -> retired. owners must attach migration plan.

tom_runtime: perf note: putting an extra hop is cheap if we implement it as a tiny hot path in the router (inline transforms, no allocations for common cases). worst-case cost is 1-2 allocations and a header map copy. we should bench it.

tom_runtime: prototyping suggestion: run coalescer in shadow mode for 2 weeks on a small percentage of traffic. measure added ns at router, plus failure modes.

sophia_ops: from rollout POV we need clear signal gating. two things: (1) opt-in tenant flag to enable coalescer for a tenant, (2) ability to pin a tenant to previous adapter path while we validate. can we keep both paths live and do mirrored outputs for a while?

ana_dev: yes — plan was: shadow transform + mirrored payload compare. not trying for instant cutover. also preserve request id so diffs are traceable.

jen_sre: SRE concerns: fallback surface and SLO. if coalescer has a bug we must auto-fail to the previous adapter path. propose a circuit-breaker rule: if coalescer error rate > 0.5% or added p99 > 5% for 5m, flip traffic back and alert on-call.

jen_sre: also add synthetic probes that exercise common transform permutations every 5m (small requests) so we catch regressions before customers do.

mike_arch: compatibility semantics — do we encode behavioral compat quirks (e.g., client expects trailing comma tolerated) or only structural rewrites (headers, payload envelope)?

ana_dev: I'd propose two classes: 1) structural normalizers (safe, always in coalescer), 2) behavioral tolerances (opt-in, experimental, with strong tests). keep behavioral cheats out unless there's broad demand.

tom_runtime: minor nit — caching implications. some transforms change cache keys (e.g., defaulting a param). we must ensure transform is applied consistently pre-cache or we risk cache poisoning. rule: transforms that change cache-affecting fields must run before cache key computation and add a transform-version tag into cache key.

ana_dev: good catch. will add transform-version field and bump on changes.

sophia_ops: observability: each transform should emit: owner, rule_id, version, matched=true/false, latency micros. make these searchable in console and part of per-route dashboard.

ana_dev: API for rules (sketch):
```yaml
- id: normalize-envelope-v1
  owner: @ana_dev
  kind: structural
  match: header X-Client-Type in ["old-sdk"]
  action: unwrap.envelope.payload
  version: 1
  ttl: 90d
```

mike_arch: governance: add a weekly "coalescer review" and automated pruning suggestions (rules with low match rate, no owner updates). keep RFCs in a dedicated folder.

jen_sre: rollback hooks please. and a small playbook: how to flip traffic, how to debug diffs (use request id to compare), how to triage if mirrored outputs diverge.

ana_dev: next steps I propose:
- internal RFC with proto API and lifecycle rules (owners, ttl, telemetry)
- bench prototype in router in shadow mode (tom)
- build console widgets for rule visibility (sophia)
- small pilot with 2 tenants that maintain old adapters (mike)

ana_dev: who wants to co-own the RFC? I can draft, but need architects and SRE to sign off.

mike_arch: I can co-author. happy to take governance section.

tom_runtime: I can bench and prototype in router. will add perf numbers in PR.

sophia_ops: will scope observability and the pilot gating UX.

jen_sre: I'll write the rollback playbook and synthetic probes.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline note: created branch "coalescer/prototype" and a gated pipeline stub (ci:6m).

ana_dev: awesome. I'll start the RFC draft today and ping the group when it's up. thanks for quick takes. :rocket:
